steps.title: Definition
steps.body: Development is the process of improvement in a country's economic and social conditions. It involves changes in wealth, health, education, and standard of living.

steps.title: Definition
steps.body: GNI per head is the total value of goods and services produced by a country in a year, plus income from abroad, divided by the population. It is measured in US dollars.

steps.title: Key Link
steps.body: Social and economic indicators are closely connected. Higher GNI means more money for healthcare and education, which leads to lower infant mortality, higher life expectancy, and better literacy rates.

steps.title: Definition
steps.body: The HDI is a composite indicator created by the United Nations that combines three measures of development: GNI per head (PPP), life expectancy at birth, and mean years of schooling.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always name specific indicators when discussing development - don't just say "it's more developed" Use data to support your answers (approximate figures for GNI, life expectancy, etc.) Remember that no single indicator gives a full picture - always evaluate limitations When describing the DTM, always refer to specific stages and explain the reasons for changing birth and death rates Use the terms LIC, NEE, and HIC correctly in your answers If asked to compare countries, use specific named examples with data Common error: confusing GDP and GNI - GDP is produced within borders, GNI includes income from abroad
